_readme: The single source of the narration (script v4: conversational rewrite). `text` is what the voice reads; '|' marks phrase breaks: each phrase is synthesised separately and joined with a natural pause, and captions follow the measured phrase timings. `offset` = seconds after the scene starts that the line begins.

voice.direction: Young adult female, Indian English. Conversational and human: like telling a friend the story behind something you care about. Warm, a little playful in Act 1, reflective in Act 2, bright in Act 5. Not bookish, not dramatic, not promotional.

lines.text: My first salary landed… | and honestly? It felt amazing.
Then the essentials went out — | rent, electricity, groceries, getting to work. | And whatever was left… was up to me.
Save it? Invest it? Insurance? | I had no clue where to start.
And I wondered — was it just me? | My semester project became the perfect excuse to find out.
First, I looked at the apps. | Most assumed you already knew what you were doing.
Then I talked to people — over forty of them. | Then twenty-three deeper conversations with early-career professionals, twenty-one to twenty-six. | I wasn't alone.
Some leaned on a friend. | Some googled everything. | Some kept it in bits and pieces. | Some felt awkward asking. | Everyone needed a different place to start.
And it's not just investing. | Spending, saving, emergencies, insurance — | there's a lot to learn, and no rush.
Most apps just want you to act. | I wanted to help people understand first.
And that's how Stack Up started.
You get practice money — | a safe place to explore, practise, even mess up.
You choose where to begin — | saving, insurance, or investing. | Say you pick mutual funds.
It asks a few simple questions, | and suggests where you could start.
But it's only a suggestion. | If it doesn't feel right, pick another.
Then you try it, with practice money — | and see what your decision looks like, | without risking your actual savings.
Every step fills your Confidence Jar, | at your own pace.
Confidence isn't given. | It's built — one step at a time.
